acceptance_results.element: A new run reaches the opening-coaching flow through the supported launcher
acceptance_results.evidence: Two documented entry points, both on a genuinely new run folder (empty run dir, no run state): (1) factory.py card --step --run-dir <fresh> -> rc 0, first line 'Question 1 of 15 - PURPOSE', body carries 'What is this video for?'; (2) the same run through intake_card.py --step prints the one-time intro on call 1 and 'Question 1 of 15 - PURPOSE' on call 2. The chat sequence (intro then purposeful question 1) therefore works through the launcher the client actually gets. Purpose card total 15 vs legacy card total 14, so the flow is distinguishable by the printed count alone.
acceptance_results.counts: fresh-run purpose card: 15 questions; legacy card: 14 questions; 2/2 entry points open on PURPOSE

acceptance_results.evidence: Resumed run carrying saved work (control/state.sqlite3, card-answers.json, control/card-receipt.json) through the documented launcher: rc 0, first line 'Question 1 of 14 - OFFER', no PURPOSE anywhere in the output, control/method.json NOT created. All three pre-existing files are byte-identical before and after (sha256 compared per file). A purpose-flow run (control/method.json present) resumes on PURPOSE 15 and its method.json is unchanged. findings.title: A pre-upgrade chat run that saw its intro but answered nothing is classified differently by the two shipped entry points
findings.detail: Run state {intro_shown: true} with no intake_purpose_flow and no saved answers is a state only pre-upgrade runs can hold (current code writes intake_purpose_flow with the intro). On that exact state factory.py card -> 'Question 1 of 15 - PURPOSE' (intake_preflight/factory.py _purpose_flow_for -> _run_is_new), while intake_card.py --step and IC.conversation -> 'Question 1 of 14 - OFFER' (intake_card.new_run_flow -> _intro_shown). Proven in isolated run dirs.
findings.why_not_blocking: No acceptance element breaks: no artifact exists on that run to migrate or rewrite, and a new run (no run state) reaches PURPOSE on both entry points. The effect is a different starting question on a legacy empty run, and the purpose card is the intended upgrade for a run that has answered nothing.
findings.scope_note: intake_preflight/factory.py is outside this unit's owned_output (choice_card/intake_card/). Recorded for the judge, not fixed here.

findings.title: The 'API and launcher agree' test exercises one launcher, not both
findings.detail: test_the_api_and_the_launcher_agree_on_the_default drives intake_card.main, which is the direct CLI. It does not drive factory.py card, which SKILL.md lines 634 and 1152-1154 name as the intake launcher. Cross-entry-point agreement is therefore asserted for one pair and unproven for the pair that F1 separates.
findings.why_not_blocking: The test is honest about what it calls (IC.main) and passes; it is a coverage gap on a legacy-only state, not a weakened or false assertion.
